mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW M550i engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW M550i N63 V8 engine replacement typically costs £4,500-£8,500 for a rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £5,500-£12,000 depending on the specialist. Used engines can be found from £2,500-£5,000.

mainEntity.name: What engine codes were used in the BMW M550i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW M550i xDrive has used three N63 V8 engine codes: N63B44O2 (2017-2019, 456hp), N63B44T3 (2020-2021, 523hp, shared with M850i), and N63B44D (2021-2023, 530hp). The engine code is stamped on the engine block and can also be verified via your VIN.

The M550i's reliability depends on the engine iteration. The early N63B44O2 has a reputation for oil consumption, timing chain issues and turbocharger problems. The later N63B44T3 and N63B44D are significantly more reliable, addressing many of the early hot-vee design weaknesses.

mainEntity.name: What are the common problems with the BMW M550i engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common issues across all N63 variants are excessive oil consumption (valve stem seals), timing chain stretch and guide wear, cooling system leaks, and turbo oil feed line failures. The hot-vee design generates extreme under-hood heat which accelerates gasket and seal degradation.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW M550i?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your M550i's age, mileage and condition. A low-mileage 2020+ M550i (£30,000-£45,000) easily justifies replacement costs. A high-mileage 2017-2019 example (£18,000-£25,000) requires careful evaluation - assess the car's overall condition, service history and whether it's had the N63 customer care package applied.

mainEntity.name: Can I still find parts for the BMW M550i N63 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the N63 V8 has strong aftermarket and OEM parts support in the UK. Specialists stock timing components, valve stem seals, cooling system parts, turbo oil feed lines and full rebuilt units. The N63 is shared across multiple BMW models (550i, 650i, 750i, X5, X6, X7), ensuring parts availability.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series M550i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW M550i xDrive was introduced in 2017 as the flagship M Performance model of the G30 5 Series range, sitting just below the full-fat M5. Powered by BMW's N63 4.4-litre twin-turbo V8, the M550i brought M Division-inspired performance to the executive saloon segment, offering a compelling balance of luxury, everyday usability and explosive power.

milestones.description: G30 M550i xDrive launched with N63B44O2 4.4L V8, producing 456hp (340kW) and 650Nm of torque
M550i receives the updated N63B44T3 V8 from the M850i, boosting output to 523hp (390kW) and 750Nm
Further power increase to 530hp with N63B44D variant
G30 M550i production ends; V8 engine retired from non-M 5 Series models

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series M550i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW M550i's N63 V8 is a masterpiece of engineering, delivering effortless performance. However, the 'hot-vee' design - with turbos mounted between the cylinder banks - generates extreme heat that can accelerate wear on gaskets, seals and timing components. Later N63TU3 and N63B44D variants are notably more reliable. A rebuilt M550i engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Excessive Oil Consumption - Why the BMW M550i N63 V8 Burns Oil
problems.rootCause: Valve stem seals degrade prematurely due to heat from the hot-vee turbo layout. Many owners report adding a quart of oil every 700-1,000 miles.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of valve stem seals, often including cylinder head work
repairOptions.longevity: Effective fix for oil consumption, but labour-intensive
When oil consumption is severe or other failures are present

problems.recommendation: Valve stem seal replacement is a well-documented fix for N63 oil consumption. If caught early, this is a cost-effective specialist repair. If the engine has suffered from prolonged oil starvation or other failures, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safer long-term choice.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 5 Series M550i engine prices

problems.group: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear
problems.h4: Timing Chain Stretch and Guide Wear - N63 V8 Critical Failure
problems.affectedModels: BMW 5 Series M550i (N63B44O2, earlier N63 variants)
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain guides become brittle with heat cycling, leading to chain stretch and potential catastrophic failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, guides, tensioners
repairOptions.longevity: Essential preventative maintenance on higher-mileage N63 engines
If chain has jumped or guides have failed catastrophically

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On sub-£20,000 M550i examples, timing chain guide replacement may represent 10-20% of vehicle value - a worthwhile preventative investment if the car is otherwise sound.
problems.recommendation: If you hear rattling on cold startup, have the timing chain guides inspected immediately. Preventative replacement is strongly recommended on N63 engines approaching 80,000 miles. If the chain has already jumped, a rebuilt engine is typically the most cost-effective route.

problems.group: Cooling System and Turbo Oil Feed Line Failures
problems.h4: Cooling System and Turbo Oil Feed Line Failures
problems.rootCause: Extreme under-hood heat from the hot-vee design causes plastic cooling system components to degrade, and turbo oil feed line o-rings to fail.

repairOptions.tier: Cooling system refresh + oil line replacement
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of expansion tank, hoses, thermostat, turbo oil feed lines

repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused catastrophic engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - assess whether full replacement cost justifies itself against the M550i's current market value.
problems.recommendation: Regular cooling system inspection and replacement of turbo oil feed line o-rings are essential on all N63 V8s. These are relatively inexpensive fixes that prevent catastrophic failure. If the engine has overheated badly, a rebuilt unit with warranty is the safer long-term choice.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 5 Series M550i
finalCta.paragraph: The M550i represents the pinnacle of BMW's M Performance V8 engineering. With regular preventative maintenance - particularly oil consumption monitoring, timing chain inspection and cooling system attention - your M550i can keep delivering that signature twin-turbo V8 character for years to come. If replacement is required, EnginesMarket connects you with UK specialists offering rebuilt N63 units with 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery.
